description: Comprehensive question bank on Local Government (Panchayati Raj and Urban Local Bodies) derived from FDA/SDA examination notes. Covers 73rd & 74th Amendments, Karnataka Panchayat Raj, urban local bodies, constitutional articles, schedules, reservations, tenure, elections, finance, and Karnataka legislation. Verify and expand before formal examination use.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What is local self-government?

options.A: A system where the Union Government directly administers villages
options.B: A system in which elected institutions at village, town and city levels manage local affairs and provide civic and developmental services
options.C: A system where State Government officers manage all local affairs without elected bodies
options.D: A system of judicial administration at the local level

questions.explanation: Local self-government is a system in which elected institutions at village, town and city levels manage local affairs and provide civic and developmental services. It decentralises decision-making and enables people to participate directly in governance.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Why is local government important in Indian democracy?

options.A: It concentrates power in the Union Government
options.B: It replaces the State Legislature
options.C: It brings administration closer to residents, enables local participation, identifies area-specific needs, supports service delivery, encourages accountability and gives effect to democratic decentralisation
options.D: It eliminates the need for constitutional amendments

questions.explanation: Local government brings administration closer to residents, enables local participation, identifies area-specific needs, supports service delivery, encourages accountability and gives effect to democratic decentralisation.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which constitutional provisions establish local self-government in India?

options.A: Part IX (Articles 243-243O) for Panchayats and Part IXA (Articles 243P-243ZG) for Municipalities
options.B: Part III (Articles 12-35) for Panchayats and Part IV (Articles 36-51) for Municipalities
options.C: Part V (Articles 52-151) for Panchayats and Part VI (Articles 152-237) for Municipalities
options.D: Part X (Articles 244-244A) for Panchayats and Part XI (Articles 245-263) for Municipalities

questions.explanation: Part IX (Articles 243-243O) deals with Panchayats and was inserted by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992. Part IXA (Articles 243P-243ZG) deals with Municipalities and was inserted by the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: In which list of the Seventh Schedule does local government fall?

options.B: State List (List II)

questions.explanation: Local government is Entry 5 of the State List (List II) in the Seventh Schedule. State legislatures therefore make the principal laws governing Panchayats and Municipalities, subject to the Constitution.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What is the difference between rural and urban local government?

options.A: Rural local government is organised through Municipal Corporations; urban local government through Gram Panchayats
options.B: Rural local government is organised through Panchayati Raj Institutions (Gram Panchayat, Taluk/Intermediate Panchayat, Zilla Panchayat); urban local government through urban local bodies (Nagar Panchayats, Municipal Councils, Municipal Corporations)
options.C: Both are organised through the same institutions
options.D: Rural local government is under the Union Government; urban local government is under the State Government

questions.explanation: Rural local government is organised through Panchayati Raj Institutions - Gram Panchayat, Taluk/Intermediate Panchayat and Zilla Panchayat in Karnataka. Urban local government is organised through urban local bodies such as Nagar Panchayats, Municipal Councils and Municipal Corporations.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What is the constitutional significance of the 73rd and 74th Amendments?

options.B: They gave constitutional recognition to rural and urban local bodies, prescribed regular elections and five-year terms, provided reservations, established State Election Commissions and State Finance Commissions, and created constitutional frameworks for devolution of powers and responsibilities
options.C: They transferred all local government subjects to the Union Government
options.D: They made local body elections optional

questions.explanation: The 73rd and 74th Amendments gave constitutional recognition to rural and urban local bodies, prescribed regular elections and five-year terms, provided reservations, established State Election Commissions and State Finance Commissions, and created constitutional frameworks for devolution of powers and responsibilities.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: When was the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act passed and brought into force?

options.A: Received Presidential assent on 20 April 1993 and came into force on 24 April 1993
options.B: Received Presidential assent on 26 January 1992 and came into force on 15 August 1992
options.C: Received Presidential assent on 1 June 1993 and came into force on 1 July 1993
options.D: Received Presidential assent on 24 April 1992 and came into force on 20 April 1993

questions.explanation: The Constitution (Seventy-third Amendment) Act, 1992 received Presidential assent on 20 April 1993 and came into force on 24 April 1993. National Panchayati Raj Day is observed on 24 April.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: National Panchayati Raj Day is observed on which date?

options.B: 24 April

questions.explanation: National Panchayati Raj Day is observed on 24 April, the date the 73rd Amendment came into force in 1993.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which Parts and Schedules were added by the 73rd Amendment?

options.B: Part IX, titled 'The Panchayats', comprising Articles 243 to 243O, and the Eleventh Schedule listing 29 subjects

questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment inserted Part IX, titled 'The Panchayats', comprising Articles 243 to 243O, and added the Eleventh Schedule, which lists 29 subjects that may be devolved to Panchayats by State law.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What is the purpose of Article 243A?

options.A: It provides for reservation of seats in Panchayats
options.B: It recognises the Gram Sabha and allows the State Legislature to provide by law for its powers and functions at the village level
options.C: It provides for State Finance Commission
options.D: It provides for duration of Panchayats

questions.explanation: Article 243A recognises the Gram Sabha and allows the State Legislature to provide by law for its powers and functions at the village level.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What is a Gram Sabha under Article 243(b)?

options.A: The elected executive body at the village level
options.B: The body consisting of persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village within the area of a village-level Panchayat

questions.explanation: Gram Sabha is the body consisting of persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village within the area of a village-level Panchayat. It is the foundational forum for direct participation in rural local governance.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What is the three-tier Panchayati Raj system?

options.A: Village level, taluk level and state level
options.B: Village level, intermediate or block level, and district level
options.C: Gram Sabha, Gram Panchayat and Zilla Panchayat
options.D: Village level, district level and state level

questions.explanation: The three-tier Panchayati Raj system consists of the village level, intermediate or block level, and district level. In Karnataka these tiers are Gram Panchayat, Taluk Panchayat and Zilla Panchayat.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Is the intermediate-level Panchayat compulsory in every State?

options.A: Yes, every State must constitute it
options.B: No, a State with a population not exceeding 20 lakh may choose not to constitute Panchayats at the intermediate level
options.C: No, it is optional only for Union Territories
options.D: Yes, but only in States with population above 50 lakh

questions.explanation: No. Article 243B provides that a State with a population not exceeding 20 lakh may choose not to constitute Panchayats at the intermediate level.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What is the normal duration of a Panchayat?

options.B: Four years
options.C: Five years from the date appointed for its first meeting unless sooner dissolved under law

questions.explanation: Under Article 243E, every Panchayat continues for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting unless sooner dissolved under law. Elections to reconstitute it must be completed before expiry of its term.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What happens if a Panchayat is dissolved before the expiry of five years?

options.A: No election is required until the original term ends
options.B: An election to constitute the new Panchayat must ordinarily be completed within six months of dissolution; if the remainder of the original term is less than six months, an election for that short remainder is not required
options.C: The State Government administers the Panchayat for the remaining term

questions.explanation: An election to constitute the new Panchayat must ordinarily be completed within six months of dissolution. If the remainder of the original term is less than six months, an election for that short remainder is not required. The newly constituted Panchayat serves the remainder of the original term.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What reservation is constitutionally provided in Panchayats under Article 243D?

options.B: Reservation of seats for SCs and STs in proportion to their population in the Panchayat area, and reservation of not less than one-third of the total seats for women, including women belonging to SCs and STs; not less than one-third of chairperson offices at each level are also reserved for women
options.C: Reservation of 50% for women and 25% for SC/ST
options.D: No reservation is provided in Panchayats

questions.explanation: Article 243D provides reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in proportion to their population in the Panchayat area, and reservation of not less than one-third of the total seats for women, including women belonging to SCs and STs. Not less than one-third of chairperson offices at each level are also reserved for women. State law may provide reservation for backward classes.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Does the Constitution itself prescribe 50 per cent reservation for women in all Panchayats?

options.A: Yes, the Constitution mandates 50 per cent
options.B: No, the constitutional minimum is not less than one-third; a State may provide a higher percentage by law. Karnataka has provided 50 per cent reservation for women through State legislation
options.C: No, the Constitution does not provide any reservation for women
options.D: Yes, but only for SC/ST women

questions.explanation: No. The constitutional minimum is not less than one-third. A State may provide a higher percentage by law. Karnataka has provided 50 per cent reservation for women in Panchayat Raj Institutions through State legislation.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which Article deals with State Election Commissions for Panchayat elections?

options.B: Article 243K

questions.explanation: Article 243K vests the superintendence, direction and control of preparation of electoral rolls and conduct of Panchayat elections in the State Election Commission. The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor and has constitutionally protected conditions of service and removal.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which Article provides for State Finance Commissions for Panchayats?

options.B: Article 243I

questions.explanation: Article 243I requires the Governor to constitute a Finance Commission every fifth year to review the financial position of Panchayats and recommend principles for sharing State revenues, grants-in-aid and measures to improve their financial position.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What does Article 243G provide?

options.A: It provides for reservation of seats
options.B: It enables the State Legislature to endow Panchayats with powers and authority necessary to function as institutions of self-government, including preparation of plans for economic development and social justice and implementation of schemes relating to Eleventh Schedule subjects
options.C: It provides for duration of Panchayats
options.D: It bars court interference in electoral matters

questions.explanation: Article 243G enables the State Legislature to endow Panchayats with powers and authority necessary to function as institutions of self-government, including preparation of plans for economic development and social justice and implementation of schemes relating to Eleventh Schedule subjects.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What does Article 243H provide?

options.B: It enables State Legislatures to authorise Panchayats to levy, collect and appropriate taxes, duties, tolls and fees; assign State revenues to them; provide grants-in-aid; and establish Panchayat funds, as prescribed by State law
options.C: It provides for State Election Commission
options.D: It provides for reservation of chairperson offices

questions.explanation: Article 243H enables State Legislatures to authorise Panchayats to levy, collect and appropriate taxes, duties, tolls and fees; assign State revenues to them; provide grants-in-aid; and establish Panchayat funds, as prescribed by State law.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What does Article 243J provide?

options.A: It allows the State Legislature to make provisions by law for maintenance of Panchayat accounts and their audit
options.B: It provides for reservation of seats for SC/ST
options.C: It provides for duration of Panchayats
options.D: It provides for powers of Panchayats

questions.explanation: Article 243J allows the State Legislature to make provisions by law for maintenance of Panchayat accounts and their audit.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What does Article 243O provide?

options.A: It provides for State Finance Commission
options.B: It bars court interference in specified electoral matters relating to Panchayats; delimitation laws cannot be questioned in court in the manner barred by the Article, and Panchayat elections can be challenged only through an election petition presented as provided by State law
options.C: It provides for reservation of women
options.D: It provides for Gram Sabha powers

questions.explanation: Article 243O bars court interference in specified electoral matters relating to Panchayats. Delimitation laws cannot be questioned in court in the manner barred by the Article, and Panchayat elections can be challenged only through an election petition presented as provided by State law.

questions.explanation: The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects that may be devolved to Panchayats by State law.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a subject in the Eleventh Schedule?

options.B: Minor irrigation and water management

questions.explanation: Urban planning including town planning is a subject in the Twelfth Schedule (for Municipalities), not the Eleventh Schedule. questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following is included in the Eleventh Schedule?

options.B: Urban forestry

questions.explanation: Poverty alleviation is one of the 29 subjects in the Eleventh Schedule. Fire services, urban forestry, and regulation of slaughterhouses are subjects in the Twelfth Schedule for Municipalities.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following is a subject in the Eleventh Schedule?

questions.question: Which of the following is included in the Eleventh Schedule?

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Does the Eleventh Schedule automatically transfer all 29 subjects to Panchayats?

options.A: Yes, all 29 subjects are automatically transferred
options.B: No, the Eleventh Schedule identifies subjects for possible devolution; Article 243G leaves the actual powers, responsibilities, functions, funds and functionaries to be provided by State legislation and government action
options.C: Yes, but only for States with population above 20 lakh
options.D: No, the subjects are transferred only after a Presidential order

questions.explanation: No. The Eleventh Schedule identifies subjects for possible devolution. Article 243G leaves the actual powers, responsibilities, functions, funds and functionaries to be provided by State legislation and government action.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which law governs the Panchayati Raj system in Karnataka?

options.B: The Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993 (Karnataka Act 14 of 1993), as amended

questions.explanation: The Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993 (Karnataka Act 14 of 1993), as amended, provides the principal State-law framework for rural local self-government.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What is the three-tier Panchayati Raj structure in Karnataka?

options.A: Gram Sabha, Taluk Panchayat and Zilla Panchayat
options.B: Gram Panchayat at village level, Taluk Panchayat at taluk/intermediate level, and Zilla Panchayat at district level
options.C: Gram Panchayat, Municipal Council and Municipal Corporation
options.D: Village Panchayat, Block Panchayat and State Panchayat

questions.explanation: The three tiers in Karnataka are Gram Panchayat at village level, Taluk Panchayat at taluk/intermediate level, and Zilla Panchayat at district level.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: When did Karnataka bring its Panchayat Raj legislation into force after the 73rd Amendment?

options.A: Karnataka enacted the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Act, 1993, which came into effect on 10 May 1993; it was later renamed the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993 with effect from 25 February 2016
options.B: Karnataka enacted the Act in 1994, effective from 1 January 1994
options.C: Karnataka enacted the Act in 1992, effective from 24 April 1993
options.D: Karnataka enacted the Act in 2000, effective from 1 April 2000

questions.explanation: Karnataka enacted the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Act, 1993, which came into effect on 10 May 1993. It was later renamed the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993 with effect from 25 February 2016.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What is a Gram Panchayat?

options.A: The body of all registered voters in a village
options.B: The elected local self-government institution at the village or group-of-villages level

questions.explanation: A Gram Panchayat is the elected local self-government institution at the village or group-of-villages level. It provides local civic services, implements rural development programmes and undertakes functions assigned under the Constitution and Karnataka law.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What is the Gram Sabha's relationship with the Gram Panchayat?

options.A: The Gram Sabha is the elected executive body and the Gram Panchayat is the body of voters
options.B: The Gram Sabha is the body of registered voters of the relevant village area, whereas the Gram Panchayat is the elected executive local body
options.C: Both are elected bodies with identical functions
options.D: The Gram Panchayat appoints the Gram Sabha members

questions.explanation: The Gram Sabha is the body of registered voters of the relevant village area, whereas the Gram Panchayat is the elected executive local body. Gram Sabha meetings provide a forum for public participation, review of works, discussion of local priorities and social accountability under State law.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What are the major functions of a Gram Panchayat?

options.B: Village sanitation, drainage, street lighting, drinking-water facilities, maintenance of local roads and community assets, registration-related functions assigned by law, implementation of rural development and welfare schemes, and preparation of village development plans
options.C: Only implementation of Central Government schemes
options.D: Only maintenance of law and order

questions.explanation: Depending on statutory devolution, Gram Panchayat functions include village sanitation, drainage, street lighting, drinking-water facilities, maintenance of local roads and community assets, registration-related functions assigned by law, implementation of rural development and welfare schemes, and preparation of village development plans.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What is a Taluk Panchayat?

options.B: The intermediate-tier rural local-government institution for a taluk

questions.explanation: A Taluk Panchayat is the intermediate-tier rural local-government institution for a taluk. It coordinates and supports Gram Panchayats, plans and implements development programmes at taluk level, and performs functions assigned by the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act and State rules.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What are the major functions of a Taluk Panchayat?

options.B: Coordinating Gram Panchayat plans and programmes, implementing assigned rural development and welfare schemes, monitoring works and services at taluk level, supporting technical and administrative coordination, and preparing or consolidating plans as required by law

questions.explanation: Taluk Panchayat functions include coordinating Gram Panchayat plans and programmes, implementing assigned rural development and welfare schemes, monitoring works and services at taluk level, supporting technical and administrative coordination, and preparing or consolidating plans as required by law.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What is a Zilla Panchayat?

options.B: The taluk-level Panchayat

questions.explanation: A Zilla Panchayat is the district-level rural local-government institution. It coordinates district-level rural development planning and implementation and performs the powers and responsibilities assigned by State law.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What are the major functions of a Zilla Panchayat?

options.B: District-level planning and coordination of rural development programmes, supervision and review of schemes, allocation or monitoring of resources as provided by law, coordination with Taluk Panchayats and Gram Panchayats, and delivery of services entrusted to it

questions.explanation: Zilla Panchayat functions include district-level planning and coordination of rural development programmes, supervision and review of schemes, allocation or monitoring of resources as provided by law, coordination with Taluk Panchayats and Gram Panchayats, and delivery of services entrusted to it.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Are Gram, Taluk and Zilla Panchayats independent sovereign governments?

options.B: No, they are constitutionally recognised institutions of local self-government, but their powers, functions, finances and administrative arrangements operate within the Constitution and State legislation
options.C: Yes, they are independent of the State Government
options.D: No, they are field offices of the State Government

questions.explanation: No. They are constitutionally recognised institutions of local self-government, but their powers, functions, finances and administrative arrangements operate within the Constitution and State legislation.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Who conducts elections to Karnataka Gram, Taluk and Zilla Panchayats?

options.B: The Karnataka State Election Commission

questions.explanation: The Karnataka State Election Commission conducts and supervises elections to Panchayati Raj Institutions under Article 243K and applicable State law.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: How are Panchayat finances supported in Karnataka?

options.B: Through local taxes, fees and other revenues authorised by State law, assigned State revenues, grants-in-aid, and transfers recommended through the State Finance Commission framework under Articles 243I and 243H

questions.explanation: Panchayat finances in Karnataka may be supported through local taxes, fees and other revenues authorised by State law, assigned State revenues, grants-in-aid, and transfers recommended through the State Finance Commission framework under Articles 243I and 243H.

questions.explanation: The 74th Amendment inserted Part IXA, titled 'The Municipalities', comprising Articles 243P to 243ZG, and added the Twelfth Schedule containing 18 subjects for possible devolution to urban local bodies.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which Article provides for the constitution of Municipalities?

options.B: Article 243Q

questions.explanation: Article 243Q provides for three types of Municipalities: Nagar Panchayat for a transitional area, Municipal Council for a smaller urban area, and Municipal Corporation for a larger urban area. Industrial townships may be specified in the circumstances provided by the Article.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What is a Nagar Panchayat?

options.A: An urban local body for a larger urban area
options.B: An urban local body for an area in transition from rural to urban status
options.C: A rural local body at the village level

questions.explanation: A Nagar Panchayat is an urban local body for an area in transition from rural to urban status, as classified under Article 243Q and State law.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What is a Municipal Council?

options.A: An urban local body for a larger urban area
options.B: An urban local body for a smaller urban area
options.C: A rural local body at the taluk level

questions.explanation: A Municipal Council is an urban local body for a smaller urban area. In Karnataka, municipal councils are commonly classified as Town Municipal Councils or City Municipal Councils under State law, depending on the category and applicable statute.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What is a Municipal Corporation?

options.A: An urban local body for a transitional area
options.B: An urban local body for a smaller urban area
options.C: An urban local body for a larger urban area
options.D: A rural local body at the district level

questions.explanation: A Municipal Corporation is an urban local body for a larger urban area. It is responsible for civic administration and urban services within its jurisdiction, under the applicable State municipal corporation law.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What factors are considered when classifying an area as transitional, smaller urban or larger urban?

options.B: Population, population density, revenue generated for local administration, percentage of employment in non-agricultural activities, economic importance and other relevant factors

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which principal laws govern urban local bodies in Karnataka?

options.A: The Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993 only
options.B: The Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 and the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, together with amendments, rules and special legislation applicable to particular urban areas
options.C: The Karnataka Local Authorities Act, 1985 only
options.D: The Karnataka Urban Development Act, 2000 only

questions.explanation: The Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 and the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 have traditionally provided the main statutory frameworks for different classes of urban local bodies, together with amendments, rules and special legislation applicable to particular urban areas.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What are the main categories of urban local bodies in Karnataka?

options.A: Gram Panchayat, Taluk Panchayat and Zilla Panchayat
options.B: Town Panchayats/Nagar Panchayats for transitional or smaller urbanising areas, Town Municipal Councils, City Municipal Councils and Municipal Corporations

questions.explanation: The State's urban local government framework includes Town Panchayats/Nagar Panchayats for transitional or smaller urbanising areas, Town Municipal Councils, City Municipal Councils and Municipal Corporations, as classified under applicable State law and notifications.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What is the difference between a Town Municipal Council and a City Municipal Council?

options.A: There is no difference; they are the same
options.B: Both are municipal councils, but they apply to different classes of urban areas under State law; their classification depends on statutory criteria and government notifications, and exact population or revenue thresholds should be checked against the current amended law and notification
options.C: Town Municipal Councils are rural bodies and City Municipal Councils are urban bodies
options.D: City Municipal Councils are under the Union Government and Town Municipal Councils are under the State Government

Their classification depends on statutory criteria and government notifications; their exact population or revenue thresholds should be checked against the current amended law and notification.

questions.subject: Local Government

questions.subject: Local Government

questions.question: Are local bodies part of the State Government department hierarchy?

options.B: No, they are institutions of local self-government, not simply field offices of State departments; however, their powers, finances, staff and functions are governed by the Constitution, State legislation, rules and lawful State supervision

questions.explanation: The Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 has traditionally provided the main statutory framework for Municipalities in Karnataka.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What is a Town Panchayat/Nagar Panchayat in Karnataka?

options.A: An urban local body for transitional or smaller urbanising areas
options.B: An urban local body for larger urban areas
options.C: A rural local body at the village level

questions.explanation: The State's urban local government framework includes Town Panchayats/Nagar Panchayats for transitional or smaller urbanising areas.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a category of urban local body in Karnataka?

options.B: Town Municipal Council

questions.explanation: Zilla Panchayat is a rural local-government institution at the district level, not an urban local body. The urban local body categories in Karnataka include Town Panchayats/Nagar Panchayats, Town Municipal Councils, City Municipal Councils and Municipal Corporations.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function typically assigned to urban local bodies?

options.A: Urban planning and regulation of land use
options.B: Water supply and sanitation
options.C: Solid waste management and public health
options.D: Conducting elections to the State Legislative Assembly

questions.explanation: Conducting elections to the State Legislative Assembly is the responsibility of the Election Commission of India, not urban local bodies. Urban local body functions include urban planning, regulation of land use, water supply, sanitation, solid waste management, public health, street lighting, parks, fire services, slum improvement, poverty alleviation, public amenities and registration of births and deaths.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: A municipal councillor represents which territorial unit?

options.B: A taluk

questions.explanation: A councillor represents a municipal ward, participates in council meetings and committees, raises local issues, scrutinises budgets and proposals, and helps communicate residents' needs to the municipal administration.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Who implements municipal decisions and administers the municipal establishment?

options.B: The Municipal Commissioner

questions.explanation: The Commissioner is the chief executive or administrative officer responsible for implementing municipal decisions and administering the municipal establishment under the applicable law.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which constitutional Article empowers the State Election Commission to supervise municipal electoral rolls and elections?

options.B: Article 243ZA

questions.explanation: Under Article 243ZA, the State Election Commission supervises and controls municipal electoral rolls and elections, including elections to corporations and municipal councils.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What does the District Planning Committee prepare?

options.A: A draft development plan for the district as a whole
options.B: A draft budget for the State

questions.explanation: Article 243ZD requires a District Planning Committee in every State district to consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities and prepare a draft development plan for the district as a whole.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What does the Metropolitan Planning Committee prepare?

options.A: A draft development plan for a metropolitan area, taking account of plans prepared by Municipalities and Panchayats within that area and matters of common interest
options.B: A draft budget for the State

questions.explanation: Article 243ZE provides for a Metropolitan Planning Committee to prepare a draft development plan for a metropolitan area, taking account of plans prepared by Municipalities and Panchayats within that area and matters of common interest.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Under which constitutional Articles does the Karnataka State Election Commission exercise its powers?

options.B: Articles 243I and 243Y

questions.explanation: The Karnataka State Election Commission exercises constitutional powers under Articles 243K and 243ZA.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Under which constitutional Articles does the Karnataka State Finance Commission function?

options.B: Articles 243I and 243Y

questions.explanation: The Karnataka State Finance Commission functions under Articles 243I and 243Y, reviewing the financial position of Panchayats and Municipalities and recommending principles for sharing State revenues, assignment of taxes, grants-in-aid and measures to improve local-body finances.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the nature of local bodies in India?

options.B: They are institutions of local self-government governed by the Constitution, State legislation, rules and lawful State supervision
options.C: They are field offices of State Government departments
options.D: They are fully controlled by the Union Government

questions.explanation: Local bodies are institutions of local self-government, not simply field offices of State departments. However, their powers, finances, staff and functions are governed by the Constitution, State legislation, rules and lawful State supervision.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What does deconcentration mean?

options.A: Transfer of meaningful functions, authority and resources to elected local governments
options.B: Redistribution of administrative tasks within the same government hierarchy
options.C: Transfer of specified tasks to another authority while retaining substantial control

questions.explanation: Deconcentration redistributes administrative tasks within the same government hierarchy.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What does delegation mean?

options.A: Transfer of meaningful functions, authority and resources to elected local governments
options.B: Redistribution of administrative tasks within the same government hierarchy
options.C: Transfer of specified tasks to another authority while retaining substantial control

questions.explanation: Delegation transfers specified tasks to another authority while retaining substantial control.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: What does devolution mean?

options.A: Transfer of meaningful functions, authority and resources to elected local governments
options.B: Redistribution of administrative tasks within the same government hierarchy
options.C: Transfer of specified tasks to another authority while retaining substantial control

questions.explanation: Devolution transfers meaningful functions, authority and resources to elected local governments.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a provision of the 73rd Amendment?

options.B: Five-year term for Panchayats
options.D: Establishment of the Election Commission of India

questions.explanation: The Election Commission of India was established under Article 324 of the Constitution, not by the 73rd Amendment. The 73rd Amendment provided constitutional recognition to Panchayats, prescribed regular elections and five-year terms, provided reservations, and established State Election Commissions and State Finance Commissions.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a provision of the 74th Amendment?

options.B: Five-year term for Municipalities
options.C: Establishment of Ward Committees in Municipalities with a population of three lakh or more
options.D: Establishment of the Union Public Service Commission

questions.explanation: The Union Public Service Commission was established under Article 315 of the Constitution, not by the 74th Amendment. The 74th Amendment provided constitutional recognition to Municipalities, prescribed regular elections and five-year terms, provided reservations, established Ward Committees, and created constitutional frameworks for devolution of powers and responsibilities.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Eleventh Schedule is correct?

options.A: It automatically transfers all 29 subjects to Panchayats
options.B: It identifies subjects for possible devolution; actual powers, responsibilities, functions, funds and functionaries are provided by State legislation and government action
options.C: It lists 18 subjects for devolution to Panchayats

questions.explanation: The Eleventh Schedule identifies subjects for possible devolution. Article 243G leaves the actual powers, responsibilities, functions, funds and functionaries to be provided by State legislation and government action.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Twelfth Schedule is correct?

options.A: It automatically vests all 18 subjects in Municipalities
options.B: It enables State Legislatures to devolve powers and responsibilities by law; actual assignment, staffing, funding and administrative control depend on State legislation and implementation
options.C: It lists 29 subjects for devolution to Municipalities

questions.explanation: Article 243W enables State Legislatures to devolve powers and responsibilities by law. Actual assignment, staffing, funding and administrative control depend on State legislation and implementation.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about reservation in Panchayats and Municipalities is correct?

options.A: The Constitution mandates 50 per cent reservation for women in all local bodies
options.B: The constitutional minimum is not less than one-third of seats for women; State laws may provide a higher percentage, as Karnataka has done with 50 per cent in Panchayat Raj Institutions
options.C: There is no constitutional reservation for SCs and STs in local bodies
options.D: Reservation for backward classes is mandated by the Constitution itself

questions.explanation: The constitutional minimum is not less than one-third of seats for women, including seats reserved for women belonging to SCs and STs. State laws may provide a higher percentage. Karnataka has provided 50 per cent reservation for women in Panchayat Raj Institutions through State legislation. Reservation for backward classes may be provided by State law.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the tenure of local bodies is correct?

options.A: Panchayats have a five-year term but Municipalities have a three-year term
options.B: Both Panchayats and Municipalities ordinarily have a five-year term; elections must be completed before expiry, and after premature dissolution elections must ordinarily be held within six months, subject to the exception where the remainder of the term is less than six months
options.C: Both Panchayats and Municipalities have a six-year term
options.D: The tenure of local bodies is determined by the Union Government

questions.explanation: Both Panchayats and Municipalities ordinarily have a five-year term. Their elections must be completed before expiry, and after premature dissolution elections must ordinarily be held within six months, subject to the constitutional exception where the remainder of the term is less than six months.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

options.A: State Election Commission - recommends local-body financial devolution
options.B: State Finance Commission - conducts Panchayat and municipal elections
options.C: State Election Commission - conducts Panchayat and municipal elections; State Finance Commission - reviews local-body finances and recommends fiscal devolution and grants
options.D: Election Commission of India - conducts Panchayat elections

questions.explanation: The State Election Commission conducts Panchayat and municipal elections. The State Finance Commission reviews local-body finances and recommends fiscal devolution and grants.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Gram Sabha and Gram Panchayat is correct?

options.A: Gram Sabha is the elected body and Gram Panchayat consists of all voters
options.B: Gram Sabha consists of all persons registered in the electoral rolls of the village area; Gram Panchayat is the elected village-level local-government institution
options.C: Both are elected bodies with identical functions
options.D: Gram Sabha is at the taluk level and Gram Panchayat is at the district level

questions.explanation: Gram Sabha consists of all persons registered in the electoral rolls of the village area; Gram Panchayat is the elected village-level local-government institution.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.topic: Zilla Panchayat vs District Planning Committee
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Zilla Panchayat and District Planning Committee is correct?

options.A: Zilla Panchayat is a planning body and District Planning Committee is a rural local-government institution
options.B: Zilla Panchayat is a rural local-government institution at district level; the District Planning Committee is a constitutional planning body under Article 243ZD that consolidates rural and urban local plans for the district as a whole
options.D: Zilla Panchayat is an urban body and District Planning Committee is a rural body

questions.explanation: Zilla Panchayat is a rural local-government institution at district level. The District Planning Committee is a constitutional planning body under Article 243ZD that consolidates rural and urban local plans for the district as a whole.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about wards and population thresholds is correct?

options.A: The Constitution prescribes exact ward numbers for each Karnataka municipality
options.B: The Constitution provides the broad framework; detailed classification, ward delimitation and local-body composition are determined by State legislation, rules and government notifications, subject to constitutional requirements
options.C: Ward numbers are determined by the Election Commission of India
options.D: Population thresholds are fixed by the Union Government

questions.explanation: The Constitution provides the broad framework. Detailed classification, ward delimitation and local-body composition are determined by State legislation, rules and government notifications, subject to constitutional requirements.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules is correct?

options.A: The subjects in both Schedules are automatically transferred to local bodies
options.B: They are subjects in respect of which State Legislatures may devolve powers and responsibilities; effective devolution requires State laws, rules, funds, functionaries and administrative implementation
options.C: The Eleventh Schedule applies to Municipalities and the Twelfth Schedule applies to Panchayats

questions.explanation: They are subjects in respect of which State Legislatures may devolve powers and responsibilities. Effective devolution requires State laws, rules, funds, functionaries and administrative implementation.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a tier of the Panchayati Raj system in Karnataka?

options.B: Taluk Panchayat

questions.explanation: Municipal Corporation is an urban local body, not a tier of the Panchayati Raj system. The three tiers in Karnataka are Gram Panchayat, Taluk Panchayat and Zilla Panchayat.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of a Gram Panchayat?

options.B: Street lighting and drinking-water facilities
options.C: Maintenance of local roads and community assets
options.D: Conducting elections to the State Legislative Assembly

questions.explanation: Conducting elections to the State Legislative Assembly is the responsibility of the Election Commission of India. Gram Panchayat functions include village sanitation, drainage, street lighting, drinking-water facilities, maintenance of local roads and community assets, registration-related functions assigned by law, implementation of rural development and welfare schemes, and preparation of village development plans.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of a Taluk Panchayat?

options.A: Coordinating Gram Panchayat plans and programmes
options.B: Implementing assigned rural development and welfare schemes
options.C: Monitoring works and services at taluk level

questions.explanation: Conducting elections to Gram Panchayats is the responsibility of the Karnataka State Election Commission. Taluk Panchayat functions include coordinating Gram Panchayat plans and programmes, implementing assigned rural development and welfare schemes, monitoring works and services at taluk level, supporting technical and administrative coordination, and preparing or consolidating plans as required by law.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of a Zilla Panchayat?

options.A: District-level planning and coordination of rural development programmes
options.B: Supervision and review of schemes
options.C: Coordination with Taluk Panchayats and Gram Panchayats

questions.explanation: Conducting elections to Municipal Corporations is the responsibility of the Karnataka State Election Commission. Zilla Panchayat functions include district-level planning and coordination of rural development programmes, supervision and review of schemes, allocation or monitoring of resources as provided by law, coordination with Taluk Panchayats and Gram Panchayats, and delivery of services entrusted to it.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993 is correct?

options.A: It was originally enacted as the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Act, 1993 and came into effect on 10 May 1993
options.B: It was enacted in 1976
options.C: It applies only to urban local bodies
options.D: It was repealed by the 74th Amendment

questions.explanation: The Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993 was originally enacted as the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Act, 1993 and came into effect on 10 May 1993. It was later renamed with effect from 25 February 2016.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about urban local bodies in Karnataka is correct?

options.A: The Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 and the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 provide the main statutory frameworks, together with amendments, rules and special legislation
options.B: Only the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993 governs urban local bodies
options.C: Urban local bodies in Karnataka are governed solely by Central laws
options.D: There is no State legislation for urban local bodies in Karnataka

questions.explanation: The Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 and the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 have traditionally provided the main statutory frameworks for different classes of urban local bodies, together with amendments, rules and special legislation applicable to particular urban areas.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the 73rd and 74th Amendments?

options.A: The 73rd Amendment deals with Municipalities and the 74th Amendment deals with Panchayats
options.B: The 73rd Amendment inserted Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule; the 74th Amendment inserted Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule
options.C: Both Amendments inserted the same Part and Schedule
options.D: The 73rd Amendment inserted Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule; the 74th Amendment inserted Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule

questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment inserted Part IX (Articles 243-243O) and the Eleventh Schedule (29 subjects) for Panchayats. The 74th Amendment inserted Part IXA (Articles 243P-243ZG) and the Twelfth Schedule (18 subjects) for Municipalities.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about reservation of chairperson offices in local bodies is correct?

options.A: No chairperson offices are reserved for women
options.B: Not less than one-third of chairperson offices at each level are reserved for women in Panchayats, and not less than one-third of chairperson offices are reserved for women in Municipalities
options.C: All chairperson offices are reserved for women
options.D: Chairperson offices are reserved only for SC/ST candidates

questions.explanation: Article 243D provides that not less than one-third of chairperson offices at each level in Panchayats are reserved for women. Article 243T provides that not less than one-third of chairperson offices in Municipalities are reserved for women.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about elections to local bodies is correct?

options.A: Elections to Panchayats and Municipalities are conducted by the Election Commission of India
options.B: Elections to Panchayats are conducted under Article 243K and to Municipalities under Article 243ZA, both by the State Election Commission
options.C: Elections to Panchayats are conducted by the Union Government and to Municipalities by the State Government
options.D: Elections to local bodies are conducted by the District Collector

questions.explanation: Elections to Panchayats are conducted under Article 243K and to Municipalities under Article 243ZA, both by the State Election Commission.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about local body finance is correct?

options.A: Local bodies have no power to levy taxes
options.B: State Legislatures may authorise Panchayats and Municipalities to levy, collect and appropriate taxes, duties, tolls and fees; assign State revenues; provide grants-in-aid; and establish funds, as prescribed by State law
options.C: Local bodies are funded only by the Union Government

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the State Finance Commission is correct?

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the State Election Commission is correct?

options.B: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor and has constitutionally protected conditions of service and removal
options.C: The State Election Commission is a temporary body
options.D: The State Election Commission conducts elections to the State Legislative Assembly

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following is a subject in the Eleventh Schedule?

options.B: Animal husbandry, dairying and poultry

questions.question: Which of the following is a subject in the Twelfth Schedule?

questions.question: Which of the following is included in the Eleventh Schedule?

questions.question: Which of the following is a subject in the Eleventh Schedule?

options.B: Social and farm forestry

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the 73rd Amendment is correct?

options.A: It made the three-tier Panchayati Raj system mandatory in every State without exception
options.B: It provides that a State with a population not exceeding 20 lakh may choose not to constitute Panchayats at the intermediate level
options.D: It transferred all local government subjects to the Union Government

questions.explanation: Article 243B provides that a State with a population not exceeding 20 lakh may choose not to constitute Panchayats at the intermediate level. The three-tier system is therefore not absolutely mandatory in every State without exception.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the duration and dissolution of Panchayats is correct?

options.A: A Panchayat continues for six years and cannot be dissolved
options.B: A Panchayat continues for five years unless sooner dissolved under law; after premature dissolution, elections must ordinarily be completed within six months, and if the remainder of the original term is less than six months, an election for that short remainder is not required
options.C: A Panchayat continues for five years and cannot be dissolved under any circumstances
options.D: After dissolution, the State Government administers the Panchayat for the remainder of the term

questions.explanation: Under Article 243E, every Panchayat continues for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting unless sooner dissolved under law. After premature dissolution, an election must ordinarily be completed within six months; if the remainder of the original term is less than six months, an election for that short remainder is not required.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the duration and dissolution of Municipalities is correct?

options.A: A Municipality continues for six years and cannot be dissolved
options.B: A Municipality continues for five years unless sooner dissolved under law; after premature dissolution, elections must ordinarily be completed within six months, subject to the short-remainder exception
options.C: A Municipality continues for three years
options.D: After dissolution, the Municipal Commissioner administers the Municipality permanently

questions.explanation: Under Article 243U, every Municipality continues for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting unless sooner dissolved under law. Elections must be completed before expiry; after premature dissolution, elections must ordinarily be completed within six months, subject to the short-remainder exception.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a factor mentioned in Article 243Q for classifying an area as transitional, smaller urban or larger urban?

options.B: Revenue generated for local administration
options.C: Percentage of employment in non-agricultural activities
options.D: Number of members in the State Legislative Assembly from that area

questions.explanation: Article 243Q requires the Governor to consider factors such as population, population density, revenue generated for local administration, percentage of employment in non-agricultural activities, economic importance and other relevant factors. The number of members in the State Legislative Assembly is not a factor.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Karnataka Panchayati Raj system is correct?

options.A: It has a two-tier structure consisting of Gram Panchayat and Zilla Panchayat
options.B: It has a three-tier structure consisting of Gram Panchayat, Taluk Panchayat and Zilla Panchayat
options.C: It has a four-tier structure including Ward Committees
options.D: It has a single-tier structure consisting only of Gram Panchayat

questions.explanation: The Karnataka Panchayati Raj system has a three-tier structure: Gram Panchayat at village level, Taluk Panchayat at taluk/intermediate level, and Zilla Panchayat at district level.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about urban local bodies in Karnataka is correct?

options.A: The Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 applies to Municipal Corporations and the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 applies to Municipal Councils
options.B: The Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 and the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 provide the main statutory frameworks for different classes of urban local bodies, together with amendments, rules and special legislation
options.C: Urban local bodies in Karnataka are governed only by the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993
options.D: There is a single Act governing all urban local bodies in Karnataka

questions.explanation: The Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 and the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 have traditionally provided the main statutory frameworks for different classes of urban local bodies, together with amendments, rules and special legislation applicable to particular urban areas.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the classification of urban areas in Karnataka is correct?

options.A: The Constitution prescribes exact population thresholds for each category of urban local body in Karnataka
options.B: The classification depends on statutory criteria and government notifications; exact population or revenue thresholds should be checked against the current amended law and notification
options.C: All urban areas in Karnataka are classified as Municipal Corporations
options.D: Urban local body classification is determined by the Election Commission of India

questions.explanation: The classification of urban areas into Town Panchayats/Nagar Panchayats, Town Municipal Councils, City Municipal Councils and Municipal Corporations depends on statutory criteria and government notifications. Exact population or revenue thresholds should be checked against the current amended law and notification.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993 is correct?

options.A: It was originally enacted as the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Act, 1993, came into effect on 10 May 1993, and was renamed with effect from 25 February 2016
options.B: It was enacted in 1976 and came into effect on 1 June 1993
options.C: It was enacted in 1964 and applies only to urban local bodies
options.D: It was enacted in 2016 and came into effect on 25 February 2016

questions.explanation: The Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993 was originally enacted as the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Act, 1993, came into effect on 10 May 1993, and was renamed with effect from 25 February 2016.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Karnataka State Election Commission is correct?

options.A: It conducts elections only to Gram Panchayats
options.B: It conducts elections to Panchayats and Municipalities in the State, prepares and supervises electoral rolls, and exercises constitutional powers under Articles 243K and 243ZA
options.C: It conducts elections to the State Legislative Assembly
options.D: It reviews the financial position of local bodies

questions.explanation: The Karnataka State Election Commission conducts elections to Panchayats and Municipalities in the State, prepares and supervises electoral rolls, and exercises the constitutional powers under Articles 243K and 243ZA.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the relationship between local bodies and the State Government is correct?

options.A: Local bodies are completely independent of the State Government
options.B: Local bodies are institutions of local self-government, not simply field offices of State departments; however, their powers, finances, staff and functions are governed by the Constitution, State legislation, rules and lawful State supervision
options.C: Local bodies are field offices of State Government departments
options.D: Local bodies are controlled directly by the Union Government

questions.explanation: Local bodies are institutions of local self-government, not simply field offices of State departments. However, their powers, finances, staff and functions are governed by the Constitution, State legislation, rules and lawful State supervision.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes deconcentration, delegation and devolution?

options.A: Deconcentration transfers meaningful functions to elected local governments; delegation redistributes tasks within the same hierarchy; devolution transfers specified tasks while retaining control
options.B: Deconcentration redistributes administrative tasks within the same government hierarchy; delegation transfers specified tasks to another authority while retaining substantial control; devolution transfers meaningful functions, authority and resources to elected local governments
options.C: All three terms mean the transfer of functions to elected local governments
options.D: Deconcentration is for urban bodies; delegation is for rural bodies; devolution is for both

questions.explanation: Deconcentration redistributes administrative tasks within the same government hierarchy; delegation transfers specified tasks to another authority while retaining substantial control; devolution transfers meaningful functions, authority and resources to elected local governments.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Ward Committees is correct?

options.A: Ward Committees are required in every Municipality regardless of population
options.B: Ward Committees are required in Municipalities with a population of three lakh or more; State law provides for their composition and territorial area, which may consist of one or more wards
options.C: Ward Committees are required only in Municipal Corporations
options.D: Ward Committees are constituted under Article 243ZD

questions.explanation: A Ward Committee is required in a Municipality with a population of three lakh or more. State law provides for its composition and territorial area, which may consist of one or more wards. Ward Committees are provided under Article 243S.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the minimum age for membership of local bodies and legislatures is correct?

options.A: Municipality: 21 years; State Legislative Assembly: 25 years; State Legislative Council: 30 years

options.C: Municipality: 30 years; State Legislative Assembly: 25 years; State Legislative Council: 21 years
options.D: All three require a minimum age of 25 years

questions.explanation: Under Article 243V, a person must have attained 21 years of age to be qualified for election as a member of a Municipality. This differs from the minimum age of 25 years for a State Legislative Assembly and 30 years for a State Legislative Council.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the District Planning Committee is correct?

options.A: It is a rural local-government institution at the district level
options.B: It is a constitutional planning body under Article 243ZD that consolidates plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities and prepares a draft development plan for the district as a whole
options.C: It conducts elections to local bodies
options.D: It reviews the financial position of local bodies

questions.explanation: Article 243ZD requires a District Planning Committee in every State district to consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities and prepare a draft development plan for the district as a whole. It is a planning body, distinct from the Zilla Panchayat, which is a rural local-government institution.

questions.subject: Local Government

options.B: It prepares a draft development plan for a metropolitan area, taking account of plans prepared by Municipalities and Panchayats within that area and matters of common interest
options.C: It conducts elections to Municipal Corporations
options.D: It reviews the financial position of Municipalities

questions.explanation: Article 243ZE provides for a Metropolitan Planning Committee to prepare a draft development plan for a metropolitan area, taking account of plans prepared by Municipalities and Panchayats within that area and matters of common interest. It is constituted under Article 243ZE, not 243ZD.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the constitutional framework for local bodies is correct?

options.A: Local government is in the Union List
options.B: Local government is Entry 5 of the State List in the Seventh Schedule; State legislatures make the principal laws governing Panchayats and Municipalities, subject to the Constitution
options.C: Local government is in the Concurrent List
options.D: Local government is a residuary subject of the Union Government

questions.explanation: Local government is Entry 5 of the State List (List II) in the Seventh Schedule. State legislatures therefore make the principal laws governing Panchayats and Municipalities, subject to the Constitution.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Article 243G is correct?

options.A: It automatically transfers all 29 Eleventh Schedule subjects to Panchayats
options.B: It enables the State Legislature to endow Panchayats with powers and authority necessary to function as institutions of self-government, including preparation of plans for economic development and social justice and implementation of schemes relating to Eleventh Schedule subjects
options.C: It provides for reservation of seats in Panchayats
options.D: It provides for the State Finance Commission

questions.explanation: Article 243G enables the State Legislature to endow Panchayats with powers and authority necessary to function as institutions of self-government, including preparation of plans for economic development and social justice and implementation of schemes relating to Eleventh Schedule subjects. It does not automatically transfer the subjects.

questions.subject: Local Government
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Article 243W is correct?

options.A: It automatically vests all 18 Twelfth Schedule subjects in Municipalities
options.B: It enables State Legislatures to endow Municipalities with powers and responsibilities necessary to function as institutions of self-government, including preparation of plans for economic development and social justice and implementation of schemes relating to Twelfth Schedule subjects
options.C: It provides for reservation in Municipalities

questions.explanation: Article 243W enables State Legislatures to endow Municipalities with powers and responsibilities necessary to function as institutions of self-government, including preparation of plans for economic development and social justice and implementation of schemes relating to Twelfth Schedule subjects. It does not automatically vest the subjects.
